text: The Leader of Opposition stressed the scope of today's motion. Schools mean elementary and primary education for middle school students. And that the importance in such institutions, the importance that we think about of the education in such institutions is how easily the students can learn historical facts. And that in order for them to have a basic fundamental knowledge of history, it is better for schools to teach history focusing on grand figures because it's more simple and likable.

I understand that it's easy to memorize and understand history if it's taught in the traditional way, which is, I would say, memorizing the basic names, years, and events in history. But there's a problem to this. It has become too superficial, as it can be seen in exams in elementary schools or middle schools where you have to fill in the gaps of the names or years of the events. And it's become just a memorization game.

Maybe a few students in your class may love history or something, and they have their favorite characters in history, like Tetsuo Noguchi or Oda Nobunaga. But I feel like the majority of elementary or middle school students will dislike history because of the simple memorizations and the ongoing entrance exams and stuff just for that. Particularly in Japan or places where they do entrance exams. I feel like history has become a memorization subject.

It does set a basic knowledge base for the students, but it goes too long. Until high school, it's mostly memorization. And the more deep education that our leader of opposition mentioned, or research, starts from university classes, and if the student chooses to take such classes.
